DXCM.thesis_one_line: The #2 continuous glucose monitor maker is growing fast and profitably, but its stock price already assumes far faster growth than it has actually delivered.
kill_criteria: Quarterly YoY revenue growth < 8% for two consecutive quarters (deceleration below guided range).
Net new US CGM patient adds or US revenue growth turns negative for a quarter (share loss to Abbott).
Gross margin falls >200bps YoY for two consecutive quarters (competitive pricing pressure).
Adverse ruling, certification, or material settlement in the pending securities class action exceeding $200m.
FDA safety communication or recall affecting G7/Stelo sensor accuracy.
key_adverse_facts: Securities class action (Section 10(b)/20(a)) alleges undisclosed G6/G7 design changes reduced device reliability, class period Jan 2024-Sep 2025.
Intensifying CGM competition from Abbott Lingo/Libre Rio targets DexCom's newest (OTC/non-insulin) growth leg.
V1's implied 10-year growth (30.2%) is well above DexCom's own delivered 5-year growth (18.0%) and Street FY1 consensus (10.9%).
data_conflicts: V1's recorded bull_ann_return_3y for DXCM is 151% (annualised), which is implausible for a 3-year annualised return on a large, maturing device maker; treated as a likely model artefact, not a usable number.
Balance-sheet (net debt ~$0.5bn) and prior-quarter revenue/EPS figures are aggregator-sourced, not re-verified against the primary 10-Q/10-K text this pass.
DXCM.confidence_in_thesis: medium - business quality is well evidenced (Q2 2026 beat-and-raise, primary source); valuation conclusion rests partly on V1's implied-growth output, which contains a flagged anomaly, and several trailing quarters were not independently re-verified.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1 tags DXCM 'fair' but its own implied growth (30.2%) exceeds both delivered 5y growth (18.0%) and consensus (10.9%); I read this as full-to-expensive rather than fair, though we agree on direction (not cheap).

DXCM.scenario_basis: Starting adjusted EPS ~$2.60 TTM run-rate; base case mid-teens revenue growth decelerating to ~13-15% with modest margin expansion and multiple holding near 25-27x NTM P/E; bear = growth slows to high-single-digits on Abbott OTC competition with multiple compression to ~20x; bull = Stelo/international sustain high-teens growth with margin expansion supporting 30x+.

EBAY.thesis_one_line: eBay's marketplace is genuinely reaccelerating on ads and niche categories like collectibles, but the stock's own next-quarter guide points to slower growth than it just delivered.
kill_criteria: FX-neutral GMV growth < 8% for two consecutive quarters (below the low end of the FY2026 outlook range).
Advertising revenue growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Consolidated net leverage (net debt/EBITDA) exceeds 3.0x on the next 10-Q.
Adverse US or EU regulatory action specifically targeting de-minimis/tariff treatment of cross-border marketplace parcels quantified by eBay as a material revenue headwind.
Non-GAAP operating margin falls below 26% for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: eBay's own Q3 2026 guide (10-12% FXN GMV growth) implies deceleration from Q2 2026's 14% FXN growth.
Consolidated Debt/Equity is elevated (~163%, aggregator-sourced), reflecting years of debt-funded buybacks against a shrinking equity base.
Tariff/de-minimis policy risk to cross-border, historically China-sourced seller categories is a live, unresolved sector-wide headwind not fully quantified in the sources reviewed.
data_conflicts: V1's carried 'delivered_5y_or_actual_roe' of 1.5% is inconsistent with a company generating the margins eBay reports; almost certainly an artefact of low/negative book equity from buybacks rather than weak true returns on capital, not resolved this pass.

Triage (Q02) argues 16.5x NTM P/E 'no longer looks demanding' post-beat; V1 still tags EBAY 'demanding' with a wide bear/bull spread (-34.9%/+72.0% annualised) - I side with V1's caution given the guided deceleration.
EBAY.confidence_in_thesis: medium - Q2 2026 results and Q3 guide are primary-source; prior seven quarters, SBC%, and FCF conversion were not independently re-verified, and tariff/de-minimis exposure was not quantified from eBay's own risk-factor disclosure this pass.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Agree with V1's 'demanding' tag: implied 10-year growth (10.5%) exceeds trailing consensus (6.7%) and eBay's own Q3 guide already points to deceleration from Q2's strength, so the recent beat does not, on its own, make the stock cheap.

EBAY.scenario_basis: Starting non-GAAP EPS run-rate ~$6.20/yr (annualised from $1.60 Q2); base case FXN GMV/revenue growth decelerating toward 8-10% (per Q3 guide) with flat ~16-17x NTM P/E; bear = growth reverts to low-single-digits (tariff/de-minimis or focus-category demand cooling) with multiple compression to ~11-12x; bull = ad take-rate and focus-category mix keep growth at 12%+ and re-rate the multiple toward the 19.4x peer median. No meaningful dividend; buybacks continue in all scenarios but excluded from these price-return figures.

ETR.thesis_one_line: A Gulf Coast power utility with a large, contracted pipeline of AI data-center customers that pay their own way, priced fairly for that growth if the deals actually get signed.
kill_criteria: 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut below the current $4.25-$4.45 range at any subsequent quarterly release.
Signed/contracted hyperscale data-center load pipeline falls below 5 GW (from the current 7-12 GW range) as disclosed in a future release.
Any state PSC formally rejects or materially amends the Fair Share Plus cost-allocation framework for a signed data-center deal.
Consolidated Debt/Equity exceeds 2.3x on a subsequent 10-Q.
NRC issues a 'yellow' or 'red' significance finding at any Entergy-operated nuclear unit.
key_adverse_facts: Two NRC 'white' (low-to-moderate significance) enforcement findings in 2026, at Grand Gulf (30 Apr) and River Bend (17 Aug) nuclear stations.
Consolidated Debt/Equity (~1.96x, aggregator-sourced) is above the regulated-utility industry median (~0.975x), funding a reported $57bn capex plan.
The 7-12 GW hyperscale pipeline is largely a pipeline, not yet fully signed/rate-based; the conversion rate to firm contracted load was not quantified in the sources reviewed.
data_conflicts: No V1 row exists for ETR; v1_verdict is null. My own reverse-DCF sense-check (implied growth ~9-10% at ~23x current-year adjusted EPS) sits close to, not clearly below, management's own >8% guided CAGR, which is why this is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than a full-weight INCLUDE.

The exact 25-Sep-2026 closing price was not confirmed against a primary exchange print; secondary-source quotes in late September clustered in the $99-102 range and this was used as an approximation, labelled as such.
ETR.confidence_in_thesis: medium - guidance and the data-center pipeline figures are primary-source (earnings release/call); the 8-quarter results table, exact closing price, and pipeline signed-contract conversion rate were not independently verified this pass.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No systematic V1 valuation exists for ETR (no row in v1_valuation_table.csv); my own reverse-DCF puts implied growth (~9-10%) at or slightly below management's own >8% long-term guided CAGR, so the reservation named for INCLUDE-SMALL is execution/regulatory risk on the pipeline, not an obvious valuation red flag.

ETR.scenario_basis: Starting 2026 guided adjusted EPS midpoint $4.35 plus ~3% dividend yield; base case EPS growth ~8% (per guidance) with P/E holding near 22-23x; bear = data-center pipeline conversion disappoints and/or a PSC rejects cost recovery, growth reverts to sector-typical 5-6% with multiple compression to ~18x; bull = pipeline converts faster than guided, growth accelerates toward low double digits with multiple holding at ~23-24x.
